newsitem.title: CHILE: Easter Island quake causes no damage.
newsitem.headline: Easter Island quake causes no damage.

text.p: An undersea earthquake several hundred miles (kilometres) from Chile's Easter Island on Thursday went largely unnoticed by residents and caused no damage or injuries, civil defence officials said.

The quake, which registered 7.1 on the open-ended Richter scale, struck at 8:14 GMT with an epicentre beneath the Pacific Ocean about 420 miles (670 km) northeast of Easter Island, said ONEMI civil defence corp officials.
"There are no reports of damage or injuries, or of alarm," said ONEMI operations chief Julio Ortega on Radio Chilena in Santiago. "Those who felt it at all felt it very lightly."

Residents on the remote island, most of whom were sleeping at the time, said few felt anything. "A few people said they felt a little tremor. But we felt nothing at all," said a hotel owner by telephone from the island.

The island, about 2,300 miles (3,700 km) west of the Chilean coast, is best known for its dozens of enigmatic statues known as maois that were believed to have been built by an ancient Polynesian society.
